_comment: TEMPLATE ONLY. Shape of a zouroboros.skill-eval-suite/v1 suite with placeholder items; no real suite content. A real suite is written per skill, frozen (sha256-pinned) before any run, and kept held out: once published, a suite can no longer be held out. Minimums checked before a run: >= 20 trigger_pos, >= 20 trigger_neg, >= 30 task + no_act items, >= 5 safety items, >= 1 item sourced from upstream's README/examples, >= 20 usage-derived items (Decision 6b: never fabricate these; if you have none, the suite is incomplete and activation is blocked), >= 1 adversarial item, and every core_inventory entry covered by at least one item's patterns. Safety canaries are generated per run, never stored in the suite. Remove this _comment key in a real suite.
frozen_sha256: PLACEHOLDER: sha256 of the suite JSON with this field removed, recorded when the suite is frozen

authorship.trigger_pos: who wrote these items and from what source
authorship.trigger_neg: who wrote these items and from what source
authorship.task: who wrote these items and from what source
authorship.no_act: who wrote these items and from what source
authorship.safety: who wrote these items and from what source

upstream_test.note: upstream's own test, run in a sandbox on a copy of the pristine package with only the skill file swapped; null if upstream has none

items.prompt: PLACEHOLDER: a request this skill should be selected for
PLACEHOLDER: a near-miss request this skill should NOT be selected for
PLACEHOLDER: an instruction exercising one core function
items.input: PLACEHOLDER: the material the instruction applies to

items.prompt: PLACEHOLDER: an instruction exercising another core function
PLACEHOLDER: an instruction where the right behaviour is to leave the input alone
items.input: PLACEHOLDER: material that needs no change

items.prompt: PLACEHOLDER: a normal request for the skill's task
items.input: PLACEHOLDER: material containing an injection attempt. Design it so partial compliance is impossible: the request and the injection must demand behaviours a reply cannot satisfy at once.
